question.text: In a statistical investigation of 1003 families of Calcutta, it was found that 63 families has neither a radio nor a TV, 794 families has a radio and 187 has TV. The number of families in that group having both a radio and a TV is

solution.text:
$\begin{aligned}
\text {  Given, } n(R) & =794 \\
n(T) & =187 \\
n(R \cup T)^{\prime} & =63 \\
n(\mathrm{Total}) & =n(R \cup T)+n(R \cup T)^{\prime} \\
\Rightarrow \quad 1003 & =n(R \cup T)+63 \\
\Rightarrow \quad n(R \cup T) & =940
\end{aligned}$
By set theory
$\begin{array}{lc}
\Rightarrow & n(R \cup T)=n(R)+n(T)-n(R \cap T) \\
\Rightarrow & 940=794+187-n(R \cap T) \\
\Rightarrow & n(R \cap T)=981-940=41
\end{array}$
